rationale: Steam explicitly states content is 'licensed, not sold' with 'no title or ownership' (Section 2.A), but uses purchase language in marketing contexts and buries this critical fact deep in a 40+ page dense legal document. The real damage comes from unilateral termination rights ('at any time'), binding arbitration, class action waivers eliminating collective recourse, unilateral amendment power, and comprehensive liability disclaimers—a stack of aggressive clauses that render theoretical ownership distinctions irrelevant.
